story_review.one_viewing_summary: This is the planned A chain, not observed pixels. A flooding San Antonio yard reaches a fence post's ankle mark before the phone's late warning. The prototype station charges from the sun, needs no tower and watches the water with four lenses that light as it rises. Its own chip lights an amber risk lamp without any server, and its radio carries to a hub, where a responder reads a spreading flood map. On a curb notice board the whole 98.82% card and its assessments tag stay readable, a blank field result card slides in, and in the wider two-card view a hand stamps none reported on it while the figure stays in frame. A finger then reads a blank map, and a technician latches the plan into the prototype's case.
story_review.opening_to_ending: The film opens on whether a station can judge rising street water with no power line or cell tower. It answers yes as a disclosed design through charge, sensing, on-chip judgment, radio and the hub map. It shows its limits plainly, with the reported validation figure kept whole beside a blank field result stamped none reported. It ends on the plan kept with an uninstalled prototype, so no deployment outcome is invented.
story_review.weakest_transition: The s7 to s8 cut at 49.2 s is the weakest. It moves from the large single validation card to a wider, almost still two-card board, where only the hand and stamp move. The phone review must show that this reads as the same board pulled wider and that the near-hold does not stall before the map cut.
